message.content:
**LangChain** is an open‑source framework designed to simplify building applications powered by Large Language Models (LLMs). It provides reusable components—called *chains*—that let developers combine LLM prompts, memory, retrieval systems, APIs, and other logic into end‑to‑end workflows without having to write everything from scratch.

Key features:

| Feature | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| **Prompt Templates & Chains** | Reusable prompt patterns that you feed data into; chains orchestrate multiple steps such as calling different models or services. |
| **Memory Management** | Keeps track of conversation context so each turn feels natural and coherent. |
| **Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)** | Integrates external knowledge sources (e.g., vector stores, databases) so the model can fetch relevant facts before answering. |
| **Tool Calling / Agentic Behavior** | Lets the LLM decide when to call external APIs or perform actions like web searches, file I/O, etc. |
| **Modular Architecture** | Plug-and-play connectors for popular LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere), embeddings engines, and storage backends. |
| **Extensibility** | You can create custom chain types, callbacks, logging hooks, and even new “tools” tailored to your domain. |

Typical use cases include chatbots, question‑answering assistants, content generators, code helpers, and more—all built on top of one or several LLMs while keeping business logic separate and maintainable.

In short, LangChain gives developers a high‑level toolkit to compose sophisticated AI pipelines quickly, focusing on what they want the system to do rather than plumbing details.
